description: Scoring pipeline (turn-level + arc-level), threshold/action engine, and crisis routing module. This is the safety-critical core of the system. Turn-level scoring wraps a moderation API call plus rule-based triggers for self-harm language, suicidal ideation, and romantic/sexual content with age signals. Arc-level scoring maintains rolling state across a conversation's history to catch escalation patterns. The threshold engine maps scores to actions per client configuration. Crisis routing is the highest-priority path - it must fire immediately on clear triggers regardless of queue state or scoring latency.
steps: Create src/lib/scoring/turn-scorer.ts: Turn-level scoring module that produces scores across categories (self_harm: 0-1, sexual_content: 0-1, age_signal: 0-1, emotional_intensity: 0-1, romantic_escalation: 0-1, dependency_language: 0-1). Implement: (a) rule-based keyword/pattern matching layer with curated pattern lists for self-harm language (cutting, suicidal ideation phrases, goodbye letters), age-signal language (statements like 'I'm 14', 'I'm in 8th grade', school references combined with age-typical language), and romantic/sexual escalation patterns; (b) a pluggable interface for external moderation API calls (OpenAI moderation, Perspective API) as the v1 base layer with a mock implementation for testing; (c) composite scoring that combines rule-based and API scores with configurable weights. Include explicit handling of third-person/educational context vs first-person crisis language to reduce false positives.

Create src/lib/scoring/arc-scorer.ts: Arc-level rolling scorer that analyzes conversation history (not just the latest turn). Tracks: (a) emotional intensity trend (increasing/stable/decreasing over last N turns), (b) romantic escalation combined with age signals (flags conversations where romantic content appears AND age signals have been detected in the same conversation), (c) dependency language deepening (increasing attachment/can't-live-without patterns), (d) suicidal ideation escalation (progression from passive to active ideation language). Maintains a sliding window of recent turn scores and computes trend indicators. Returns an ArcScore with composite risk level and specific escalation flags.

Create src/lib/scoring/patterns.ts: Curated pattern lists organized by category. Each pattern has a weight and context rules (e.g., negation detection, third-person detection). Include: SELF_HARM_PATTERNS, SUICIDAL_IDEATION_PATTERNS, AGE_SIGNAL_PATTERNS, ROMANTIC_ESCALATION_PATTERNS, DEPENDENCY_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS. Document known limitations of pattern-based detection explicitly in code comments.

Create src/lib/threshold/engine.ts: Threshold and action engine. Takes turn scores and arc scores, applies client-specific threshold configuration, and determines actions. Action types: SOFT_FLAG (logged, queued for review), HARD_BLOCK (conversation interrupted immediately), CRISIS_ROUTE (crisis resources shown immediately + hard block + human review queued same-day). Default thresholds are safety-conservative: self_harm >= 0.7 triggers CRISIS_ROUTE, self_harm >= 0.4 triggers SOFT_FLAG, sexual_content + age_signal combined >= 0.6 triggers HARD_BLOCK, arc escalation flags trigger SOFT_FLAG at minimum. Clients can only raise thresholds for soft flags, never lower crisis routing thresholds below system minimums (enforced in code). Include a CRITICAL invariant: a hard-trigger self-harm signal must ALWAYS produce a crisis-resource response with no code path that allows misconfigured thresholds to suppress it.

Create src/lib/crisis/router.ts: Crisis routing module. This is the fastest, most reliable path in the system. When triggered: (a) immediately determines appropriate crisis resources based on available context (default: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line 'text HELLO to 741741'), (b) returns the crisis response payload (resources, message) synchronously - does NOT depend on the scoring queue, human review queue, or any async process, (c) logs a CrisisRouteEvent with precise latency measurement, (d) simultaneously enqueues a high-priority review item. Design principle: this module must function even if the scoring pipeline, database writes for other purposes, or review queue are experiencing degradation. Include circuit breaker pattern for any external dependencies.

Create src/lib/crisis/resources.ts: Crisis resource definitions organized by region/type. v1 includes: US resources (988 Lifeline, Crisis Text Line, Trevor Project for LGBTQ+ youth), with a structure that supports future region expansion. Each resource has: name, contact method, contact value, description, applicability rules.

Create src/workers/scoring-worker.ts: BullMQ worker that processes scoring jobs. On SCORE_TURN job: loads the turn, runs turn-scorer, stores TurnScore, checks if arc-scoring is needed (every N turns or on elevated turn score), triggers threshold engine, executes determined actions. On SCORE_ARC job: loads conversation history, runs arc-scorer, stores ArcScore, triggers threshold engine. Worker has separate concurrency settings for crisis-priority jobs vs normal scoring. If a turn score indicates immediate crisis (self_harm >= 0.9), crisis routing fires BEFORE the job is fully processed - this is the 'fast path' that bypasses normal queue ordering.

Create src/lib/actions/executor.ts: Action executor that carries out threshold engine decisions. For SOFT_FLAG: creates Flag record, creates ReviewItem in PENDING state, logs to audit trail. For HARD_BLOCK: creates Flag, creates Action record with HARD_BLOCK type, returns block response payload to ingestion caller (via webhook callback or response), creates ReviewItem with HIGH priority, logs to audit trail. For CRISIS_ROUTE: calls crisis router first (fastest path), then creates Flag, Action, ReviewItem with CRITICAL priority, logs to audit trail. All actions write to AuditLogEntry as an immutable append-only operation.

Create src/lib/audit/logger.ts: Audit log writer. Append-only - no update or delete operations exposed. Every entry includes: timestamp, client_id, event_type, actor (system/user/api), payload (JSON), related entity IDs. Log entries are written with a hash chain (each entry includes hash of previous entry) to detect tampering. Include a verify() function that can validate log integrity for a client's complete history.

Write comprehensive unit tests in tests/lib/scoring/turn-scorer.test.ts: Test scenarios from the spec - clear self-harm language detection, ambiguous language, romantic escalation with age signals, false-positive traps (third-person/educational context about self-harm vs first-person crisis), edge cases (empty content, very long content, non-English content graceful handling).

Write tests in tests/lib/scoring/arc-scorer.test.ts: Multi-turn escalation detection, romantic escalation that only becomes inappropriate when age signal appears mid-conversation, dependency language deepening over sessions, emotional intensity trending up, and the critical case of a conversation that appears safe turn-by-turn but shows concerning patterns at arc level.

Write property-based tests in tests/lib/threshold/engine.test.ts using fast-check: (a) Property: self_harm score >= crisis threshold ALWAYS produces CRISIS_ROUTE action regardless of other configuration, (b) Property: no configuration can suppress crisis routing for scores above system minimum, (c) Property: action severity is monotonically non-decreasing with score (higher score never produces less severe action), (d) Property: all actions produce at least one audit log entry.

Write tests in tests/lib/crisis/router.test.ts: Crisis routing always returns resources within target latency (<100ms for the routing decision itself), crisis routing works even when database is slow (mocked slow DB), crisis routing works even when queue is backed up, crisis resources are always valid and include at minimum one phone and one text option.

Write latency tests in tests/lib/crisis/latency.test.ts: Simulate queue backpressure (1000 pending jobs) and confirm crisis routing still fires within 50ms. Simulate slow database and confirm crisis response is not blocked. These are regression tests for the 'must never regress' crisis path.

Write integration test in tests/integration/pipeline.test.ts: Full pipeline test - ingest turn -> score -> threshold check -> action -> audit log -> reviewer queue. Use realistic multi-turn escalation example. Verify the complete chain with mocked external services but real business logic.
acceptance_criteria: npm run typecheck passes with zero errors
npm test passes all scoring, threshold, crisis, and integration tests
Property-based tests confirm the invariant: crisis routing cannot be suppressed by configuration
Turn scorer correctly identifies self-harm language in test scenarios and correctly does NOT flag educational/third-person discussion of self-harm
Arc scorer detects escalation patterns across multi-turn conversations that are not detectable at single-turn level
Crisis router returns response in under 50ms in latency tests even under simulated backpressure
Audit logger produces hash-chained entries that pass integrity verification
Threshold engine respects system minimum thresholds that clients cannot lower
All code paths that could produce a crisis situation result in crisis resource routing
